{{short description|Mathematical structure}}
In [[mathematics]], an '''Igusa curve''' is (roughly) a coarse [[moduli space]] of [[elliptic curve]]s in characteristic ''p'' with a level ''p'' '''Igusa structure''', where an Igusa structure on an elliptic curve ''E'' is roughly a point of order ''p'' of ''E''<sup>(''p'')</sup> generating the kernel of ''V''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''E''<sup>(''p'')</sup>&nbsp;→&nbsp;''E''.  An '''Igusa variety''' is a higher-dimensional analogue of an Igusa curve. Igusa curves were studied by [[Jun-Ichi Igusa|Igusa]]{{sfnp|Igusa|1968}} and Igusa varieties were introduced by [[Michael Harris (mathematician)|Harris]] and [[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Taylor]]{{sfnp|Harris|Taylor|2001}} for studying the [[bad reduction]] of some [[Shimura varieties]]: the [[ℓ-adic cohomology|{{math|''ℓ''}}-adic cohomology]] of Igusa varieties sheds some light on that of Shimura varieties.
